title: Lost update in wallet top-ups
root_cause: Lost update: deposit/withdraw read the balance into Python (SELECT) then wrote an absolute value (UPDATE balance = old +/- amount). Two concurrent transactions read the same old balance and both wrote back, so one update silently overwrote the other and money appeared/disappeared. Fix is atomic in-database increments with a conditional withdraw.
fix: Replaced read-modify-write with single atomic UPDATE statements: deposit uses UPDATE ... SET balance = balance + amount, withdraw uses UPDATE ... WHERE balance >= amount and checks rowcount (falling back to SELECT only to distinguish unknown account from InsufficientFunds). Row-level write lock makes concurrent updates serialize without lost updates, errors, or extra locking.

repro_report.example_violation: lost update: account 1 balance is 100100 but successful deposits add up to 103200 (initial 100000, 32x100)

checks.name: same_behaviour
checks.detail: 40 sequential requests matched the original exactly

checks.name: agent_reproduction_test
checks.detail: the agent's own reproduction test passed 3/3 runs

repro_code:
import threading

def reproduce(connect, service) -> str | None:
    AID = 1
    AMT = 100
    N = 32
    with connect() as conn:
        row = conn.execute("SELECT balance FROM accounts WHERE id = %s", (AID,)).fetchone()
        initial = row[0]
    barrier = threading.Barrier(N)
    ok = 0
    lock = threading.Lock()
    def worker():
        nonlocal ok
        with connect() as conn:
            try:
                barrier.wait(timeout=15)
            except Exception:
                return
            try:
                service.deposit(conn, AID, AMT)
            except Exception:
                return
            with lock:
                ok += 1
    threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker) for _ in range(N)]
    for t in threads:
        t.start()
    for t in threads:
        t.join()
    with connect() as conn:
        final = conn.execute("SELECT balance FROM accounts WHERE id = %s", (AID,)).fetchone()[0]
    expected = initial + ok * AMT
    if final != expected:
        return f"lost update: account {AID} balance is {final} but successful deposits add up to {expected} (initial {initial}, {ok}x{AMT})"
    return None
